gsea.ranking: Welch t, Basal-like over Luminal A

views.caveat: Welch's t-test per gene on rna_seq_v2_mrna_median_all_sample_Zscores as stored, Basal-like minus Luminal A, each patient contributing the mean of their samples; computed from three running totals per gene and cohort, so it is exact across sites. 20,006 genes tested, 14 left out (fewer than 3 patients with a value in a cohort, or no variance); q is Benjamini–Hochberg across every gene tested. The 1500 most significant genes are drawn as points, the rest as density. Z-scores are standardised within each study, so a difference is in study-specific units. A t-test on thousands of patients finds tiny differences significant — read the effect, not only the q. Enrichment is preranked GSEA on the unrounded t (Subramanian et al. 2005, weight 1), significance from 1000 random sets of the same size drawn from the same ranking, seeded by the set's name so a shared link reproduces it; p = (b+1)/(m+1) over the same-sign nulls, q is Benjamini–Hochberg across the sets tested (not GSEA's own NES-based FDR). Gene-set permutation ignores gene–gene correlation, so it is anti-conservative next to phenotype permutation, which needs patient-level values.

steps.title: Sum every gene's values
steps.detail: The diffexpr:moments query above, on “rna_seq_v2_mrna_median_all_sample_Zscores” as stored. Per gene, over the cohort's patients with a value (a patient with several samples contributes their average): n, Σv and Σv². Every gene in the profile, no individual value.

steps.title: Sum every gene's values
steps.detail: The diffexpr:moments query above, on “rna_seq_v2_mrna_median_all_sample_Zscores” as stored. Per gene, over the cohort's patients with a value (a patient with several samples contributes their average): n, Σv and Σv². Every gene in the profile, no individual value.

steps.title: Leave out genes that cannot be tested
steps.detail: A gene with fewer than 3 patients with a value in either cohort, or with no variance (Var A + Var B ≤ 1e-9 · (1 + mean A² + mean B²) — judged to a tolerance, since a constant gene's variance from the sums is rounding noise).

steps.title: Welch's t-test per gene
steps.detail: Mean A − mean B (Basal-like minus Luminal A) with each cohort's variance (Σv² − (Σv)²/n)/(n − 1); unequal-variance t, Welch–Satterthwaite df, two-sided. With thousands of patients a tiny difference is significant: read the effect too.

steps.title: Preranked gene-set enrichment (GSEA)
steps.detail: Genes ranked by the unrounded t, Basal-like over Luminal A first. Enrichment score as in Subramanian et al. 2005 with weight 1 (each member's step is |t| / Σ|t| of the members). Significance from 1000 random sets of the same size drawn from the same ranking, from a generator seeded by the set's name — so a shared link gives the same p — with p = (b + 1)/(m + 1) over the m null scores of the same sign and NES = ES / mean of those. Gene-set permutation ignores correlation between genes, so it is anti-conservative next to phenotype permutation. A set with fewer than 10 ranked members is not tested. q is Benjamini–Hochberg across the sets tested.

method.verification: Welch's t from moments matches scipy 1.18.1 ttest_ind(equal_var=False) and Benjamini–Hochberg statsmodels multipletests, to a relative 1e-6 (test/moments-golden.test.ts, test/tables-golden.test.ts); enrichment scores match gseapy 1.3.1 prerank, and NES and p match the script's port of our seeded null exactly (test/gsea-golden.test.ts).
